_meta.what: the meter's own per-model credit rates, fitted from the passive stretches already in the repository. `measured_rates` is the block tracker/credits.py reads; everything else is the working the fits show.
_meta.no_traffic: read-only arithmetic over committed files; no account was driven

measured_rates.unit: credits per input token; the output rate is output_multiplier times it

opus.why: the unit anchor: 0.6667 credits per input token (5x that per output token), which is what a credit means in this repository. The fit rescales its Opus coefficient to this figure, so every rate beside it is measured relative to it and none of them tests it. If this row is wrong every credit figure scales with it and nothing in our stretches would show it.

haiku.status: not measurable, the fits cannot separate Haiku from free: its pooled interval reaches zero
haiku.why: the highest Haiku share of any clean stretch on a fitted account is 0.257, so no fit has a stretch in which this family carries the meter movement, and none can separate its rate from the other columns'. 2 of them do return a coefficient for it, but their pooled interval runs [0.00x, 20.76x] Opus and reaches zero -- the fit saying the family's whole contribution can be explained without it. Neither the value nor that interval is published, because a published interval is priced at its midpoint where there is no value (tracker/gs_passive.py) and this one's midpoint is not a rate anything measured. The per-fit coefficients are on this record; the reference figure stands beside the row, untested by our data and used in no arithmetic.

fable.why: the fits disagree within their intervals (dave/post 1.588x Opus [1.257, 2.066], jwork/post 3.149x Opus [2.485, 4.751], jwork/pre 2.102x Opus [1.969, 2.286]), so the published rate is the median of the per-fit rates (1.4014 credits per input token, 2.102x Opus) and the interval is the union of the per-fit intervals rather than a single fit's. The data cannot say whether the family's rate moved or the five-hour window did: the window fitted on the same stretches moves the same way.

measured_rates.method: delta_pct = sum over families of (input + cache_write + 5x output) x rate, plus a cache-read column, by non-negative least squares over every clean stretch of the account and side of 2026-09-14, with the Opus coefficient rescaled afterwards to 0.6667 credits per token so the fit reads in credits. Intervals are 80% bootstrap intervals over resampled stretches. A family's rate is the median of the per-fit point estimates and its interval is the union of theirs, whether or not the fits agree (`agree` records that, and `why` says what the disagreement is). A family whose pooled interval reaches zero keeps the interval and no value: the fit cannot separate it from free.

haiku.status: not measurable, the fits cannot separate Haiku from free: its pooled interval reaches zero
